Who are the legitimaries (forced heirs) in Italy?,"['Country: Italy | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 536
536
LEGITIMARIES
Persons in whose favor the law reserves a share of inheritance or other rights in the succession are: spouse, children, ascendants.
Adopted children are equated with children.
In favor of the descendants of , who come to the succession in their stead, the law reserves the same rights that are reserved for children.', 'Country: Italy | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 565
565
CATEGORIES OF SUCCESSORS
In the legitimate succession, the inheritance devolves to the spouse, descendants, ascendants, collaterals, other relatives and the State in the order and according to the rules established in this title.', 'Country: Italy | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 553
553
REDUCTION OF THE PORTIONS OF LEGITIMATE HEIRS IN CONCURRENCE WITH LEGITIMARIES
When on the property left by the deceased all or part of the legitimate succession is opened, in the concurrence of legitimates with other successors, the portions that would be due to the latter are reduced proportionately to the extent necessary to supplement the share reserved for the legitimates, who, however, must impute to this, pursuant to ART564, what they have received from the deceased by virtue of donations or legacies.']","In Italy, the persons in whose favor the law reserves a share of the inheritance (the “legitimaries” or forced heirs) are:
- the spouse
- the children (including adopted children, who are treated as children)

- the ascendants (parents, grandparents, etc.) [Italy, Civil Code art. 536][S1].","Under Article 536 of the Italian Civil Code the persons for whom the law reserves a share of the inheritance are the spouse, the children and the ascendants. Adopted children are equated with children, and descendants who come to the succession in place of a child have the same rights.",0.9999999999,1.0,0.8571428571428571,0.8298825268236831,0.8552314846519786,q15/multi

What share of the estate is reserved to the children in Italy when there is no spouse?,"['Country: Italy | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 544
544
CONCURRENCE OF ASCENDANTS AND SPOUSE
When the person who dies leaves no children, but ascendants and the spouse, one-half of the estate is reserved for the latter, and one-fourth for the ascendants.
In the case of a plurality of ascendants, the reserve share allocated to them under the preceding paragraph is divided among them according to the criteria provided for in ART569.', 'Country: Italy | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 537
537
SHARE IN FAVOR OF CHILDREN
Except as provided in ART542, if the parent leaves a single child, one-half of the estate is reserved for the child.
If there are more children, the two-thirds share are reserved for them, to be divided equally among all the children.', ""Country: Italy | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 542
542
CONCURRENCE OF SPOUSE AND CHILDREN
If the person who dies leaves, in addition to his spouse, only one child, the latter has one-third of the estate reserved for him and another one-third belongs to the spouse.
When the children, are more than one, half of the estate is reserved for them in total and the spouse is entitled to one-fourth of the deceased's estate. The division among all children, is made in equal parts.""]","In Italy, when the deceased leaves no spouse:
* If there is **one child**, the child is entitled to **½ of the estate** [S2].

* If there are **multiple children**, they together receive **⅔ of the estate**, to be divided equally among them [S2].","Under Article 537 of the Italian Civil Code, if the parent leaves a single child, one half of the estate is reserved to the child
column2: if there are more children, two thirds are reserved to them, divided equally (Article 542 applies when there is also a spouse).",0.49999999995,1.0,1.0,0.8914798783564679,0.770359652298432,q16/multi

581

542
CONCURRENCE OF SPOUSE AND CHILDREN
If the person who dies leaves, in addition to his spouse, only one child, the latter has one-third of the estate reserved for him and another one-third belongs to the spouse.
When the children, are more than one, half of the estate is reserved for them in total and the spouse is entitled to one-fourth of the deceased's estate. The division among all children, is made in equal parts."", 'Country: Italy | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 536
536
LEGITIMARIES
Persons in whose favor the law reserves a share of inheritance or other rights in the succession are: spouse, children, ascendants.
Adopted children are equated with children.
In favor of the descendants of , who come to the succession in their stead, the law reserves the same rights that are reserved for children.']","In Italy, when the deceased leaves a spouse **together with children**, the spouse’s share is:

ARTICLE 177
OBJECT OF COMMUNITY
The goods of the communion are:
(a) property acquired by the spouses together or separately during the marriage, except for personal goods

(d) companies managed by both spouses and established after the marriage.
In the case of companies owned by one of the spouses before the marriage but managed by both, community only concerns profits and increases."", ""Country: Italy | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 179
ARTICLE 179
PERSONAL PROPERTY
They do not constitute objects of community and are personal property of the spouse:
(a) property owned by the spouse before the marriage or had a right in rem to enjoy
column5: \n(b) property acquired after marriage by way of gift or inheritance, where it is not specified in the gift deed or will that it is to be allocated to the community
column6: \n(c) property for the strictly personal use of each spouse and its accessories
column7: \n(d) property used in the exercise of the spouse's profession, except property used for the purpose of running a business forming part of the community
column8: \n(e) property obtained by way of damages as well as the pension relating to the partial or total loss of the capacity to work
column9:
(f) goods acquired with the price of the transfer of the personal property listed above or by exchange thereof, provided that this is expressly stated at the time of purchase.
The acquisition of real property, or of movable property listed in Article 2683, made after the marriage, shall be excluded from community of property, within the meaning of points (c), (d) and (f) of the preceding paragraph, where such exclusion is apparent from the deed of acquisition if the other spouse was also a party to it."", 'Country: Italy | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 211
ARTICLE 211
OBLIGATIONS OF SPOUSES CONTRACTED BEFORE MARRIAGE
The community property are liable for obligations contracted by one of the spouses before the marriage limited to the value of the property owned by that spouse before the marriage which, by agreement entered into, became part of the community of property.']","**Italy – Civil Code articles 177 & 179**

column1: *Community of property* (Art. 177) comprises:
1. **Property acquired by the spouses** (together or separately) **during the marriage**, except for personal goods
2. **Fruits of each spouse’s property** that are received and not consumed at the time the community is dissolved
3. **Fruits of a spouse’s personal activities** that still exist at the dissolution of the community
4. **Companies** that are **managed by both spouses and created after the marriage**.
For companies owned by one spouse before marriage but managed jointly, only the **profits and increases** belong to the community. [S1]
*Excluded (personal) property* (Art. 179) – these do **not** form part of the community:
- Property owned before marriage or a right in rem to enjoy it
- Property acquired after marriage by gift or inheritance (unless the deed/will specifies community allocation)
- Property for strictly personal use and its accessories
- Property used in the spouse’s profession (except business assets that are part of the community)
- Damages and pension for loss of work capacity

- Goods bought with the proceeds of the above personal assets, if expressly stated at purchase. [S2]","Under Article 177 of the Italian Civil Code the community includes: property acquired by the spouses together or separately during the marriage (except personal property)
column2: the fruits of each spouse's property received and not consumed at the dissolution
column3: the proceeds of each spouse's activity still existing at the dissolution
column4: companies managed by both spouses and established after the marriage (for companies owned by one spouse before the marriage but managed by both, only profits and increases).",0.9999999999,1.0,1.0,0.731542362669995,0.6159876203075432,q19/multi

When is the community of property between spouses dissolved in Italy?,"['Country: Italy | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 191
ARTICLE 191
DISSOLUTION OF COMMUNION
Communion is dissolved by declaration of absence or presumed death of one of the spouses, annulment, dissolution or termination of the civil effects of the marriage, legal separation, judicial separation of property, conventional change of property regime, bankruptcy of one of the spouses.
In the case of legal separation, the community of property between the spouses is dissolved at the time when the president of the court authorises the spouses to live separately, or on the date of the signing of the minutes of the consensual separation of the spouses before the president, provided that they have been approved. The order by which the spouses are authorised to live separately is communicated to the civil registrar for the purposes of recording the dissolution of the community of property.
In the case of companies managed by both spouses and established after the marriage (art 177 lett. d), the dissolution of community may be decided by agreement of the spouses, observing the form provided for in Article 162, or by public deed or by declaration in the marriage certificate.', ""Country: Italy | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 177
ARTICLE 177

(a) property acquired by the spouses together or separately during the marriage, except for personal goods
column2: \n(b) the fruits of the property belonging to each of the spouses, received and not consumed at the dissolution of community
column3: \n(c) the fruits of a spouse's personal activities provided that, at the time of the dissolution of the community of property, they still exists
column4:
(d) companies managed by both spouses and established after the marriage.
In the case of companies owned by one of the spouses before the marriage but managed by both, community only concerns profits and increases."", 'Country: Italy | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 194

The court, in relation to the needs of the children and their custody, may constitute in favour of one of the spouses the usufruct on a part of the property due to the other spouse.']","In Italy the community of property between spouses is dissolved:

column1: * by a declaration of absence or presumed death of one spouse
* by annulment of the marriage

* by legal separation (the community ends either when the president of the court authorises the spouses to live separately or on the date the minutes of the consensual separation before the president are signed and approved)
* by judicial separation of property

In legal separation it is dissolved when the court president authorises the spouses to live separately or when the minutes of the consensual separation are signed.",0.9999999999,1.0,1.0,,,q21/multi

If there are more children, the two-thirds share are reserved for them, to be divided equally among all the children.', 'Country: Italy | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 536

Persons in whose favor the law reserves a share of inheritance or other rights in the succession are: spouse, children, ascendants.
Adopted children are equated with children.

(1) Forced heirs have a right to a share of an estate that the decedent cannot freely dispose of
column2: this share shall be the statutory portion.\n(2) The statutory portion of a decedent's descendants, adoptive children, and their descendants, and of the spouse shall be a half, and the statutory portion of the other heirs a third of the portion of the estate each of them would be entitled to in accordance with the law of succession.\n(3) The rest of the estate may be freely disposed of by the testator

45
In a case where a descendant or an adoptive child who has a right to a statutory portion is heavily in debt or over-profligate, the testator may dispossess him or her of the whole or a part of the statutory portion for the benefit of the forced heir's descendants. Such a dispossession shall remain valid only when the heir dispossessed of his or her statutory portion has, at the time of inheriting, an underage child or a grandchild by a previously deceased child, or if he or she has a child of full age or a grandchild of full age by a previously deceased child, and this child or grandchild has no earning capacity.""]","**Italy**

column1: - If the deceased leaves **one child**, the compulsory (legitimate) portion is **½ of the estate**.
- If the deceased leaves **more than one child**, the compulsory portion is **⅔ of the estate**, to be divided equally among the children.
- Adopted children are treated the same as biological children. [S1][S2]
**Slovenia**
- Children (including adoptive children) are forced heirs. Their reserved (statutory) share is **½ of the portion they would receive under the ordinary rules of succession**

column1: **Comparison**
- In Italy the reserved share is expressed as a fixed fraction of the whole estate (½ for one child, ⅔ for multiple children).

- In Slovenia the reserved share is calculated as **half of whatever share the child would obtain under the normal succession rules**, meaning the exact amount depends on the overall division of the estate and can vary case‑by‑case.

Thus, Italy provides a clear, larger statutory minimum (up to two‑thirds of the estate), whereas Slovenia limits the children’s protected portion to **half of their ordinary inheritance share**, leaving a larger disposable portion for the testator.","In Italy (Art. 537) one half of the estate is reserved to a single child and two thirds to two or more children
column2: with a surviving spouse (Art. 542) one child receives one third and several children one half in total. In Slovenia (Art. 26 Inheritance Act) the statutory portion of descendants is one half of the share they would receive under intestate succession

Compare the intestate share of a surviving spouse who inherits together with children in Estonia and Slovenia.,"['Country: Estonia | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 16
ACT
16.
Spouse as intestate successor
Together with the relatives of a bequeather, the bequeather’s surviving spouse succeeds in intestacy:
1) with first order successors, equally with the share of a child of the bequeather but not to less than one-quarter of the estate
column2:
2) with second order successors, to one-half of the estate.
If there are no relatives from the first or second orders, the bequeather’s spouse succeeds to the entire estate.
In addition to his or her share of the estate, the bequeather’s spouse may request establishment of real right provided for in § 227 of the Law of Property Act on an immovable which was the matrimonial home of the spouses provided that the standard of life of the bequeather’s spouse would deteriorate due to succession.
The surviving spouse does not have a right of succession or right to preferential share if the bequeather has, before his or her death, filed a claim with a court for divorce or agreed to divorce in writing or if the bequeather was entitled, at the time of his or her death, to claim annulment of the marriage and has filed the corresponding claim with a court.', 'Country: Estonia | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 12
ACT
12.
Relatives as intestate successors
Relatives succeed in three orders.
Second order successors succeed if there are no first order successors.
Third order successors succeed if there are no first or second order successors.
The provisions concerning intestate succession by relatives are subject to the right of a bequeather’s surviving spouse to the estate provided for in § 16 of this Act.', ""Country: Estonia | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 17
ACT
17.
Right of spouse to preferential share
If a bequeather’s surviving spouse succeeds together with second order successors of the bequeather, he or she receives in addition to a share of the estate the standard furnishings of the spouses' matrimonial home as a preferential share if the objects are not accessories of an immovable.
The provisions concerning a legacy apply to the preferential share."", ""Country: Slovenia | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 33
33
EXCLUSION OF HOUSEHOLD ITEMS
(1) The surviving spouse and the decedent's descendants as well as adoptive children and their descendants who have lived in the same household with the decedent shall inherit household items intended for the fulfilment of their daily needs, such as furniture, household appliances and other household equipment, bedding and similar, but not when these objects are of high value.
(2) The items thus excluded shall not be included in the calculation of the statutory portion and the hereditary portion of the heir in question."", ""Country: Slovenia | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 24
24
AN INCREASE IN A HEREDITARY PORTION
(1) In cases where parents who do not have the necessary means of subsistence inherit together with the decedent's spouse, the court, following a claim therefrom, may decide that they shall inherit also a share of that portion of the estate to which the spouse is entitled by an Act
column3:
the court may also decide that the parents shall inherit the entire estate if its value is so low that they could suffer deprivation it the estate were to be divided.
(2) If the relationship between the decedent's parents has permanently ceased and only one of them does not have sufficient means of subsistence, the parent in question may claim an increase in his or her hereditary portion against both the spouse and the other decedent's parent.
(3) If one of the decedent's parents dies prior to the decedent, the surviving parent who has no means of subsistence may claim an increase in his or her hereditary portion against the heirs of the decedent.
(4) In making such decisions, the court shall take into account all the circumstances in each case, particularly the financial circumstances and earning capacity of the spouse and the other heirs, as well as the value of the estate."", 'Country: Slovenia | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 23
23
AN INCREASE IN A HEREDITARY PORTION
(1) If a spouse inherits together with heirs from the second order of succession, the court, following his or her claim, may decide that the spouse shall inherit also a part of that portion of the estate that would by an Act be inherited by other heirs
column4: the court may also decide that a spouse shall inherit the entire estate if the value of the estate is so low that the spouse would suffer deprivation if the estate were to be divided.\n(2) In making these decisions, the court shall take into account all the circumstances in each case, particularly the financial circumstances and earning capacities of the other heirs, as well as the value of the estate.']","In Estonia, when the surviving spouse inherits together with the bequeather’s children (who are first‑order successors), the spouse receives a share **equal to that of each child, but never less than one‑quarter of the estate** [S1].",In Estonia (§ 16 Law of Succession Act) the spouse inheriting with descendants receives a share equal to that of a child but not less than one quarter of the estate. Is the common property of spouses divided equally in Italy and in Estonia?,"['Country: Italy | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 194
ARTICLE 194
DIVISION OF COMMUNITY PROPERTY
The division of community property is performed by dividing the assets and liabilities equally.
The court, in relation to the needs of the children and their custody, may constitute in favour of one of the spouses the usufruct on a part of the property due to the other spouse.', 'Country: Italy | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 215
ARTICLE 215
SEPARATION OF PROPERTY
The spouses may agree that each of them shall retain sole ownership of the property acquired during the marriage.', 'Country: Italy | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 195
ARTICLE 195
REMOVAL OF MOVABLE PROPERTY
In the division, the spouses or their heirs are entitled to take movable property that belonged to the spouses before the community or that came to them during the community by inheritance or gift. In the absence of proof to the contrary, movable property is presumed to be part of the community.', 'Country: Estonia | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 37
37.
Division
(1) After termination of jointness of property the spouses shall divide joint property between themselves. A spouse may submit an application for the division of joint property to court already together with an action for divorce or annulment of marriage or together with an action for termination of jointness of property.
(11) The composition of joint property shall be determined as of the termination of the proprietary relationship.
(2) Until the division of joint property, the requirements for administration of joint property established in Subdivision 2 of this Subchapter shall apply to the possession, use and disposal of the joint property.
(3) Joint property shall be divided between the spouses into equal parts pursuant to the provisions concerning the termination of common ownership unless otherwise agreed.', 'Country: Estonia | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 26
26.
Principle of unity of joint property
A spouse cannot dispose of his or her share in joint property or in a single object included in joint property. A spouse does not have the right to request the division of joint property during the jointness of property.
A claim owned by spouses jointly may be set off only against a claim the satisfaction of which out of the joint property is prescribed by law or by an agreement.', 'Country: Estonia | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 69
69.
Property connected with housing of family in case of divorce
(1) At the request of a spouse, a court shall divide the objects of standard furnishings of the housing of the family which are in common ownership of the spouses fairly and rationally.
(2) An object of standard furnishings connected with the housing of the family which the spouses have acquired during marriage for a charge for use in their shared household, shall be deemed to be in the joint ownership of the spouses in the case of division of property pursuant to subsection 1 of this section unless the sole ownership of one spouse with respect to this object is proved.
(3) An object transfer into the ownership of the spouse to whom the court assigns the object. A court may require this spouse to pay fair compensation for the object to the other spouse.
(4) If one spouse or both spouses are liable for the performance of obligations related to objects specified in subsection 1 of this section as solidary obligors, a court may specify which spouse shall perform the obligation arising from the relations between them.']","Yes. In both Italy and Estonia the common (or joint) property of spouses is normally divided equally between them when the marriage ends.
- **Italy** – The division of community property is carried out by splitting the assets and liabilities equally between the spouses[S1].
- **Estonia** – The law provides that, after the termination of the proprietary relationship, joint property is divided into equal parts unless the spouses have agreed otherwise[S4].

Thus, the default rule in each country is an equal (50 / 50) split, with Estonia explicitly allowing the spouses to depart from this rule by mutual agreement.","Yes in both. In Italy (Art. 194) the assets and liabilities of the community are divided in equal parts, and the judge may grant one spouse the usufruct of part of the other's share for the needs of the children. In Estonia (§ 37) joint property is divided into equal parts unless the spouses agree otherwise.",0.7499999999625,1.0,1.0,0.9713838167919365,0.8814139996195403,q25/multi
